children: Bayer received FDA approval for Kerendia (finerenone) to reduce UACR, expected to slow CKD progression, in adults with CKD associated with type 1 diabetes.
FDA approves Kerendia for CKD in T1D
Label expansion opens a new patient population, supporting potential revenue growth for Kerendia.
Approval tied to biomarker reduction; commercial uptake may hinge on outcomes linkage and payer acceptance.
Regulatory reliance on T2D outcomes suggests faster access but leaves long-term T1D outcomes to prove.
Convenient dosing can aid adherence and market adoption versus alternatives.
Signals high unmet need and could speed market penetration discussions with payers.

This is a late-stage confirmation of Bayer’s strategy to broaden Kerendia beyond T2D CKD and HF. For a larger catalyst, evidence of hard renal outcomes and clear reimbursement wins in T1D CKD would need to emerge.
